sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact word 'steadfast' (against 'humble' and 'quiet'). No earlier card has shown or hinted at that word, so a baker can't reason it out and can only guess the wording of the line. No story card sets up the question either.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The right answer 'God' is a person, while the wrong answers 'his sling' and 'his sword' are weapons. The right answer therefore stands out, and a baker needs no reasoning to pick it.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
